script: "Real ID? I said yes. The airport turned my trip into a nightmare.". So my girlfriend and I are heading to Puerto Rico in two days. Puerto Rico is still U.S. territory, so a passport isn't a thing—just a domestic flight. I had my birthday a month ago and had to renew my driver's license. I am not the smartest crayon in the toolbox, so I assumed every new ID was already Real‑ID compliant. Two friends were flying with us, and one of them asked today if my GF and I had Real IDs. I said, "I think so." Then I saw the little text in the corner of my card that says "Not for Federal ID." My heart did a 180. Why didn't they ask when I renewed it? Why didn't I notice it? I sprinted to the BMV, got a temporary paper ID that's supposedly compliant, but in my state they only mail the real thing in 14‑28 days. TSA says paper IDs are not valid. My GF started freaking out, and I was like, "Am I even getting through TSA?" I called the automated line. It kept telling me I could pay $45 for "TSA Confirm ID" and still get through. So, what? Will I make it to Puerto Rico? --- I paid the $45 fee. I had to do an extra screening checkpoint, which took about five minutes. I made it onto the plane. And now? I am in Puerto Rico, living it up.
